_gap = split-half CV r of the free ridge readout minus a constrained readout (per-rater means over fold models; same data, halves and free readout as the sign-check table). model_basis = constraint w_pop * s with one non-negative scale PER DIMENSION in the D2 fold model's standardised 8-dim basis (= gap_free_minus_D1 of the sign-check table); rotated = the same per-dimension constraint after a random orthogonal rotation of that basis (5 rotations: mean, min, max of the dataset means); pca_basis = in the principal axes of the item features; scalar = w = c * w_pop with a single c >= 0 (does not depend on an orthogonal change of basis; a stronger constraint: it removes every deviation from the population direction, not only sign reversals). frac02 = fraction of raters with gap > 0.02. cos_neg = fraction of raters whose weight has a negative cosine with the population weight: model_basis (= frac_cos_neg of the sign-check table), after an orthogonal rotation of the standardised basis (identical; max_abs_dcos is the largest per-row difference), after rotating the raw basis and re-standardising each dimension, in the whitened basis, and as the correlation of the two readouts' predictions over the training items._

_Means over 2 seeds. tag matched = noise SD calibrated so that the est-vs-hold rho of the simulated participants (sim_splithalf; the definition of scripts/48: Spearman between the inverse-MDS RDMs of a random 70 % and the remaining 30 % of the arrangement trials, all participants) equals that of the real participants (real_splithalf), size of the individual differences as before (weight SD 0.6); tag matched_id = the size of the individual differences (wsd; eps of the D2 type follows) is calibrated as well, so that the held-out rho of the true population RDM (sim_hold_truepop) equals that of the real D0 embedding (real_hold_pop). sim = generating type, kind = fitted model; hold_* = held-out rho on the fold-0 simulated participants (pop = z = 0 of the fitted model); true_* = rho with the noiseless individual RDM. eps_at_bound = 1: the D2-type family cannot produce individual differences as large as the calibrated D1 type (rho between true and population RDM stays above about 0.37-0.39 even at the upper bound eps = 8), so the matched_id D2-type rows are NOT matched on the population rho (0.35-0.36 instead of 0.30) and are not used. Earlier conditions for comparison: noise 0.30 gave sim_splithalf 0.40 (Exp. 2) and noise 0.45 gave 0.20 (Exp. 1)._

_Paired contrasts on per-rater values (seeds averaged per rater first). mean_diff, sem (SD / sqrt n), 95 % CI from the t distribution, t and df of the paired t test, cohen_dz = mean / SD of the paired differences, p_t = two-sided paired t, p_w = two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank; p < 1e-300 underflows to 0 in the CSV. 43 of 58 rows reproduce the mean difference and n of the existing results/*_paired.csv exactly (asserted in scripts/89); the others have no row there (baseline, free-text, modal-vote and sign-check contrasts) or use more seeds (London image version: 3 seeds here, results/london_img_paired.csv has seeds 0-1 only). Source files are named in the CSV. Sign-check rows are one-sample tests of the per-rater loss against 0._

_Correlations. Spearman p values are the usual t approximation; Mantel and CCA p values are permutation p = (count + 1) / (n_perm + 1), so the smallest possible value is 1 / (n_perm + 1); rows with n_models = 20 give the mean coefficient and the median p over the 20 fold models._


## Figures (figures/INDEX.md, one panel per PDF)

- `london_z_prefmale.pdf` (3.0x2.8 in): London Set: male-face preference index (mean residual rating of male minus female faces) vs its prediction from the D1 latent z (learned-embedding version, D = 8, M = 4 main models only, 40 estimation faces). Within each fold model the index of the fold-out raters is predicted from their z by 10-fold ridge CV (z is not pooled across models because the basis differs). Plotted: the 10 fold models of seed 0, so each rater appears once (n = 2501), in the model where the rater is fold-out; dotted = identity. CV R2 per fold model = 0.71 over all 50 models (10 folds x 5 seeds; range 0.63-0.80; the value to quote) and 0.71 over the 10 plotted models (range 0.65-0.77); R2 of the plotted points pooled = 0.72. Predictions are not averaged over seeds (that ensemble gives R2 0.82 and would not match the quoted value). From results/london_z_prefmale.csv, results/london_z_prefmale_models.csv (scripts/88; redrawn 2026-11-13, the earlier version mixed in the D/M sensitivity models and gave 0.30).
